newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX EUROYEN FIRM BUT OFF HIGHS ON MACHINERY DATA.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX EUROYEN FIRM BUT OFF HIGHS ON MACHINERY DATA.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen futures were off their highs in late Friday trade after running up against technical resistance, but dealers said the market remained firm on persistent signs of weakness in Japan's economy.
The release of machinery orders data showing a 10.6 percent month-on-month drop for June lifted the lead March Euroyen contract to a high of 99.24.
"There was no follow through buying from 99.24 so people started to take profit. Everybody was looking at that as a resistance level," a trader at a European futures house said.
He said the contract could head for 99.30/31 if it breached the 99.24 level. At 1115 GMT, it stood unchanged against an IMM close of 99.21 on light volume of 4,735 lots.
Japanese government bond futures for September ended at 126.59 against their previous 126.67.
Eurodollar futures ended easier on spillover selling after U.S. treasuries ended lower overnight following a poor 30-year bond auction.
Dealers said the market was increasingly nervous about the U.S. interest rate outlook against a backdrop of recently bullish economic data.
Overnight comments by Thomas Hoenig, president of the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City, also weighed on the market, the trader said.
Hoenig said the U.S. economy carried an upside risk of inflation given the low jobless rate.
The trader said December Eurodollars faced resistance around 94.10/11, while support was likely at 94.00. They ended at 94.050 against an IMM finish at 94.070.
